newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Trading slows after volatile week.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Trading slows after volatile week.

text.p: Shares settled into a humdrum after-hours trading session Friday after a topsy-turvy week that featured a 109-point drop in the Dow Jones Industrial Average over the five-day period.
"There's really not that much to write home about," a trader said of the after-hours quiet.
Greeting card maker American Greetings posted a $0.01 quarterly dividend increase from $0.17 to $0.18 shortly before the U.S. market close, but did not trade out of line after-hours.
Elsewhere, the New York Stock Exchange suspended apparel retailer Edison Brothers Stores, which had been halted on the exchange for several weeks.
"I haven't seen anything happening," another trader said, noting that Friday's after-hours trading is often calm.

American General did not trade either, despite a late announcement by the financial services organization that it would take a second quarter after-tax charge of $26 million on the sale of its credit card portfolio.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume hit 175,400 from 1,600 the previous day; session two volume moved down to 2.6 million from 4.0 million.
